description: Apply the server banner color from FEAT-001/FEAT-002 to the Sidebar banner display. This is a small integration step that ties FEAT-001 (bannerColor field in Community type) and FEAT-002 (bannerColor saving) together with the Sidebar rendering. Independent of FEAT-003. Also performs final integration checks.
steps: In src/sections/Sidebar.tsx, in the server banner header div (around line 308), update the style to apply bannerColor when no bannerUrl is set: `style={{ backgroundColor: !activeCommunity.bannerUrl ? (activeCommunity.bannerColor || undefined) : undefined, backgroundImage: activeCommunity.bannerUrl ? url(${activeCommunity.bannerUrl}) : undefined, backgroundPosition: activeCommunity.bannerUrl ? `50% ${activeCommunity.bannerPosition ?? 50}%` : undefined }}`. Ensure the div always renders (remove the `{activeCommunity.bannerUrl && ...}` conditional guard) so the color banner also shows. If bannerColor and bannerUrl are both unset, do not render the banner div at all.

In src/components/ServerSettingsDialog.tsx overview section banner preview div, apply bannerColor as backgroundColor when serverBannerUrl is empty: add `backgroundColor: !serverBannerUrl ? (serverBannerColor || undefined) : undefined` to the preview style. This gives live preview of the chosen color.
Run `npm run build` and `node --test scripts/audit.test.mjs` to confirm all integrations are working.
acceptance_criteria: Setting a banner color in ServerSettings and saving shows the color in the Sidebar banner strip.
The Sidebar banner area does not render (no empty space) when neither bannerUrl nor bannerColor is set.
findings: Both integration points were already applied in FEAT-002: (1) Sidebar.tsx banner div conditionally renders when (bannerUrl || bannerColor), applies backgroundColor from bannerColor when no bannerUrl; (2) ServerSettingsDialog.tsx preview div applies backgroundColor: serverBannerColor && !serverBannerUrl ? serverBannerColor : fallback. Build: vite exit 0, 2567 modules, no TS errors. Tests: 1 pass, 0 fail.
